subject: State Health Dept — privacy addendum, HIPAA + DPIA (pilot)
messages:
From: Melissa Carter <melissa.carter@oregon.gov>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@oregon.gov
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Privacy addendum + DPIA for pilot with County Health

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed. We're kicking off a 6-month pilot with Clark County Health Services and procurement has asked us to get a vendor privacy addendum in place before the kickoff. Two things they flagged as blockers:

- State requirement that vendors accept a standard privacy addendum (we attach one) and any redlines go through the procurement office.
- The program lead wants confirmation about HIPAA applicability and whether you can support a DPIA / PIA summary for our internal review.

Can you confirm:
1) Whether Redwood can sign a state privacy addendum (we understand vendors sometimes propose counter-addenda).
2) If Redwood has a DPIA template or can provide a short summary of data flows, controls, and retention for the pilot.
3) Availability of evidence: SOC 2 report, completed SIG/CAIQ, and any FedRAMP-relevant controls (they flagged "FedRAMP-adjacent" requirements).

Deadline: procurement would like documentation by Friday 11/14 to meet their calendar. Is that feasible?

Appreciate any notes and a POC we can share with the procurement/legal teams.

Best,
Melissa
Program Manager — Oregon Department of Public Health

Attachment: OR_State_Privacy_Addendum_Draft.docx (state provided template)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Melissa Carter <melissa.carter@oregon.gov>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privacy addendum + DPIA for pilot with County Health

Melissa — thanks for the clear note and the template. Looping in Laura (legal) and Dev (solutions/controls) to handle the DPIA and contract questions.

Quick answers up-front:
- We can work with the state's privacy addendum but will propose a small set of redlines around audit scope and indemnity (I'll let Laura outline specifics).
- We can produce a concise DPIA summary and a data flow diagram for the pilot (PII/PHI boundaries, retention, deletion path).
- Evidence: we can share our SOC 2 Type II attestation, a completed SIG Lite spreadsheet, and a short mapping of Redwood controls to FedRAMP controls (note: not FedRAMP-certified).

I will aim to get the draft vendor addendum + evidence bundle to you by EOD Thursday 11/13 to give your team time. If procurement needs Friday 11/14 that's tight but potentially OK.

Next steps: Laura, Dev — see Melissa's template attached. Can you: 1) mark required contract redlines, 2) produce the DPIA one-pager + data flow, 3) confirm exact evidence we can provide by Thu EOD?

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

--

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privacy addendum + DPIA for pilot with County Health

Team — reviewed the state's template. High-level notes:

1) Acceptable with redlines: primary asks will be to narrow the audit scope (we should limit to production systems used for the pilot), clarify data subject rights handling, and add standard carve-outs for subcontractors that have limited data access.
2) HIPAA: if the pilot involves PHI we need a BAA-like clause; state template appears to assume a combination of PHI and sensitive public health data. We'll propose adding BAA language and references to our encryption/segregation controls.
3) DPIA: Dev — please prepare a 1-page DPIA summary (data categories, lawful basis, risk level, mitigating controls) and a simple diagram. I will draft the counter-addendum (RDW redlines) and attach internally.
4) Evidence: we can provide: SOC 2 Type II attestation (2024-2025 period), completed SIG questionnaire (redacted), CAIQ summary, and a control mapping to FedRAMP Moderate (informational only). For anything marked "restricted" we'll propose an NDA or a secure share link.

Timeline: I can get a redline and short note to Rishi by EOD Wed (11/12). Dev — can you target Thu EOD for the DPIA summary and the technical note on data residency, logging, and access controls?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Legal-Redlines-Checklist.pdf

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privacy addendum + DPIA for pilot with County Health

Laura / Rishi — DPIA one-pager & technical control summary attached. Highlights:

- Data flows: ingest -> transient KV cache (auto-evicted) -> model infer -> ephemeral outputs stored in customer-owned bucket (configurable). For the pilot we recommend no long-term retention of inbound payloads unless explicitly enabled.
- PHI handling: encryption at rest (AES-256), in-transit (TLS1.3), role-based access controls, logging with 365-day retention by default (can be extended).
- SCCs/SCC-equivalent: Redwood can support SCC-style contractual safeguards for cross-border transfers; for this US state pilot transfers are within US regions, except occasional analytics processing in EU staging — we'll keep any EU movement opt-in only.
- FedRAMP adjacency: controls mapped to FedRAMP Moderate where practical; we will not claim FedRAMP authorization but provide a controls mapping.

Attached: DPIA-Summary-OR-Pilot.pdf; Tech-Control-Notes-Redwood.pdf; SIG-Questionnaire-Completed.xlsx

Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks,
Rishi

One more ask: procurement will run a short risk assessment. If you have a 1-page summary that maps your controls to the state's key sections (Data Residency, Encryption, Access Controls, Logging & Retention) that would help speed up their decision.

I'll follow up Monday with any procurement redlines. Talk soon.

Best,
Melissa
